svg.title: Covering Index
svg.desc: Covering Index. Answer a query from the index alone: include the columns it selects, so the table is never read, and the scan is index-only. Step 1, One heap page per row: The index finds the 20 newest entries on one leaf page, then reads 20 heap pages to return the rows. Step 2, INCLUDE: index-only scan: INCLUDE (id, status, total_thb) puts the selected columns in every leaf entry: an Index Only Scan. Step 3, The visibility map decides: An UPDATE clears 3 pages' visibility bits: Heap Fetches 4. After VACUUM, Heap Fetches is 0 again. Step 4, Costs and other engines: Twice the size, costlier writes. InnoDB entries carry the primary key; SQL Server has INCLUDE too.

g.text: The index finds the 20 newest entries on one leaf page, then reads 20 heap pages to return the rows.
INCLUDE (id, status, total_thb) puts the selected columns in every leaf entry: an Index Only Scan.
An UPDATE clears 3 pages' visibility bits: Heap Fetches 4. After VACUUM, Heap Fetches is 0 again.
Twice the size, costlier writes. InnoDB entries carry the primary key; SQL Server has INCLUDE too.
All 20 entries sit on one leaf
page, but each points to its row
key. Without it the plan stayed
it had to check in the heap.
status sits in an index now
Backward scan: newest entry first; an entry is key + tid
Each leaf entry now carries id, status and total_thb
New entries (purple); the scan marked the old ones dead
one leaf entry: 24 bytes → 56 bytes; per leaf page: 261 → 122
INCLUDE columns are not in the root or internal pages
The 3 columns as key columns also give 32 MB here.
INCLUDE keeps a UNIQUE index unique on its key alone
and accepts types with no B-tree operator class.
One row needed, one whole page read.
The 20 rows sit on 20 pages spread
The scan reads 1 visibility map page
instead: every page bit is set, so each
entry is answered from the index alone.
VACUUM sets a bit when all rows on the
page are visible to everyone; any change
is a Filter, not an Index Cond
With only 2 dead rows it skipped the
index pass: 2392 and 4806 keep a dead
stub until a later vacuum, and the scan
Every entry carries the primary key, so
SELECT id is covered. There is no
INCLUDE: add status, total_thb as key
The clustered index is the table, so a
lookup by id lands on the row itself.
Included columns sit at the leaf level
only; the clustering key rides along.
A column the index lacks costs one
